option_description: Whether the running firmware/build is affected by an unpatched CISA KEV-listed CVE for this appliance family (FortiOS CVE-2024-21762, PAN-OS CVE-2024-3400, Ivanti CVE-2023-46805/CVE-2024-21887, Citrix Bleed CVE-2023-4966), covering both the auth-bypass/RCE chain and the memory-disclosure session-token-leak primitive.
security_impact: Primary OR-trigger of "Unpatched KEV appliance exploit (auth-bypass / RCE chain)" and also referenced by "Session token theft bypassing MFA" (the Citrix-Bleed memory-disclosure primitive); the exposure fires when true (the running build is affected by an unpatched KEV CVE).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Capture the appliance model and running firmware/build so it can be compared against vendor advisories and the CISA KEV catalog.
how_to_obtain.command: show system status / get system status (FortiGate) | show version (Cisco ASA) | show system info (PAN-OS) — capture model + firmware/build
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Version compared against vendor advisory + CISA KEV; an affected build is a finding
how_to_obtain.source: CISA BOD 22-01 Known Exploited Vulnerabilities

how_to_obtain.instruction: Cross-check the captured running build against KEV entries for the platform family.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Cross-check the running build against KEV entries for the platform (FortiOS CVE-2024-21762/CVE-2022-40684, PAN-OS CVE-2024-3400, Ivanti CVE-2023-46805/CVE-2024-21887, Citrix CVE-2023-4966).
how_to_obtain.source: Threat Actors Exploit Multiple Vulnerabilities in Ivanti Connect Secure and Policy Secure Gateways (CISA AA24-060B)

option_description: Whether the appliance runs an end-of-support / end-of-life firmware image that no longer receives security fixes, meaning newly disclosed KEV CVEs will never be patched on this build.
security_impact: One of the OR-triggers for "Unpatched KEV appliance exploit (auth-bypass / RCE chain)"; fires when true (build is past its security-fix support window).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Capture the running firmware branch/build to compare against the vendor's lifecycle dates.
how_to_obtain.command: show system status / get system status (FortiGate) | show version (Cisco ASA) | show system info (PAN-OS) — capture model + firmware/build
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Version compared against vendor advisory + CISA KEV; an affected build is a finding
how_to_obtain.source: CISA BOD 22-01 Known Exploited Vulnerabilities

how_to_obtain.instruction: Check the captured firmware branch against the vendor's published end-of-support / end-of-life lifecycle dates.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Running branch is within its vendor security-fix support window (secure); a branch past its EoL/EoS date is a finding.
how_to_obtain.source: general-knowledge

option_description: Number of days since the gateway firmware was last updated. Internet-facing VPN appliances are mass-exploited shortly after disclosure, so a stale patch cadence is itself an exposure proxy.
security_impact: An OR-trigger for "Unpatched KEV appliance exploit (auth-bypass / RCE chain)"; fires when the value exceeds the 90-day patch-currency threshold.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Read the running firmware build and its install/upgrade date from the appliance status/update history, then compute days elapsed to today.
how_to_obtain.command: show system status / get system status (FortiGate) | show version (Cisco ASA) | show system info (PAN-OS) — capture model + firmware/build
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Version compared against vendor advisory + CISA KEV; an affected build is a finding
how_to_obtain.source: CISA BOD 22-01 Known Exploited Vulnerabilities

how_to_obtain.instruction: Determine the install/upgrade date of the running image from the appliance update/upgrade history and compute days elapsed.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Days since last firmware update is small (recently patched, e.g. <90); a large value indicates a stale patch cadence.
how_to_obtain.source: general-knowledge

option_description: Idle timeout (minutes) for an established authenticated VPN/admin session before it is terminated. A long or absent idle timeout widens the window in which a stolen session token (e.g. Citrix Bleed CVE-2023-4966) can be replayed.
security_impact: An OR-trigger for "Session token theft bypassing MFA"; fires when above a tight bound (>15 minutes).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Read the admin and SSL-VPN idle-timeout settings and record the value in minutes.
how_to_obtain.command: config system global; show | grep admintimeout  (FortiGate). Harden: 'set admintimeout 5'. SSL-VPN: 'config vpn ssl settings' -> 'set idle-timeout'/'set auth-timeout'
how_to_obtain.expected_output: admintimeout small (e.g. 5) and SSL-VPN idle/auth timeouts set (secure) vs large/disabled (insecure)
how_to_obtain.source: FortiGate Hardening Guide — System administrator best practices

how_to_obtain.instruction: On non-FortiGate platforms, locate the vendor-equivalent SSL-VPN/admin idle-timeout setting and record minutes.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Idle session timeout is short (~5 min, <=15); no idle timeout / very long sessions is a finding.
how_to_obtain.source: general-knowledge

option_description: Maximum absolute lifetime (hours) of an authenticated session/token regardless of activity. Long-lived or never-expiring sessions let a hijacked token persist indefinitely after the leak, even post-patch.
security_impact: An OR-trigger for "Session token theft bypassing MFA"; fires when above a bounded maximum (>24h).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Read the absolute session/auth-timeout setting and record the value in hours.
how_to_obtain.command: config system global; show | grep admintimeout  (FortiGate). Harden: 'set admintimeout 5'. SSL-VPN: 'config vpn ssl settings' -> 'set idle-timeout'/'set auth-timeout'
how_to_obtain.expected_output: admintimeout small (e.g. 5) and SSL-VPN idle/auth timeouts set (secure) vs large/disabled (insecure)
how_to_obtain.source: FortiGate Hardening Guide — System administrator best practices

how_to_obtain.instruction: On non-FortiGate platforms, locate the vendor-equivalent absolute auth/session-timeout setting and record hours.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: A bounded re-authentication interval (<=24h); never-expiring or multi-day sessions is a finding.
how_to_obtain.source: general-knowledge

option_description: Whether active VPN sessions are monitored for anomalous source/geo/parallel use and exported to SIEM so a hijacked session can be detected and revoked.
security_impact: An OR-trigger for "Session token theft bypassing MFA"; fires when monitoring is absent (false).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Confirm session/connection logs are exported off-box so live session inventory can be monitored centrally.
how_to_obtain.command: show log syslog/forwarding config (FortiGate 'config log syslogd setting' -> 'set status enable' + server; PAN-OS log-forwarding profile to syslog)
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Remote syslog/SIEM target configured and enabled (secure) vs logging off or local-only (insecure)
how_to_obtain.source: FortiGate Hardening Guide — System administrator best practices

how_to_obtain.instruction: Confirm SIEM has detections for anomalous session sources/geo/concurrency for this gateway.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Log content and retention meet NIST SP 800-92; SIEM has detections for failed-auth bursts and anomalous session sources.
how_to_obtain.source: NIST SP 800-92 Guide to Computer Security Log Management

option_description: Whether a per-user concurrent-session cap is enforced, constraining a hijacked-token attacker logging in parallel with the legitimate user and aiding detection of anomalous duplicate sessions.
security_impact: An OR-trigger for "Session token theft bypassing MFA"; fires when no cap is enforced (false).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Check the VPN portal settings for a per-user concurrent-connection / single-login limit.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: VPN settings show a per-user concurrent-connection limit; anomalous parallel sessions reviewed as part of remote-access policy.
how_to_obtain.source: NIST SP 800-46 Rev. 2 - Guide to Enterprise Telework, Remote Access, and BYOD Security

how_to_obtain.instruction: Where the platform exposes it, read the per-user concurrent-session setting from the SSL-VPN portal config.
how_to_obtain.command: config vpn ssl web portal; show (FortiGate — review 'limit-user-logins' / per-portal login cap); PAN-OS GlobalProtect gateway 'Agent > Client Settings' max user sessions
how_to_obtain.expected_output: A non-zero per-user concurrent-session cap is set (secure) vs unlimited concurrent sessions per identity (insecure)
how_to_obtain.source: general-knowledge

option_description: Whether multi-factor (ideally phishing-resistant) authentication is enforced for ALL remote-access VPN logins with no exception groups.
security_impact: The defining OR-trigger of "Valid-account abuse / missing MFA"; fires (insecure) when login is single-factor/password-only or MFA is optional/bypassable, so stolen/sprayed/stuffed credentials alone grant External Remote Services access.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Inspect the VPN authentication policy for mandatory MFA across every realm/portal with no exception groups.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Auth policy shows every VPN realm/portal requires a second factor (RADIUS/SAML push, TOTP, or certificate); no exception groups. Verify phishing-resistant factors per CISA fact sheet.
how_to_obtain.source: CISA Implementing Phishing-Resistant MFA fact sheet

how_to_obtain.instruction: Confirm the authentication assurance level meets NIST AAL2+ for remote access.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Authentication assurance level meets NIST SP 800-63B AAL2+ for remote access; memorized-secret-only flows flagged.
how_to_obtain.source: NIST SP 800-63B Rev 4 — Digital Identity Guidelines: Authentication

option_description: Whether account lockout / login throttling (non-zero lockout threshold + duration, bounded SSH grace time) is configured on the public VPN portal and admin interface.
security_impact: An OR-trigger for both "Valid-account abuse / missing MFA" and "Internet-exposed management interface / default credentials"; fires (insecure) when there is no lockout / unlimited attempts, allowing unblunted password spraying and credential stuffing.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Read the admin lockout threshold/duration and SSH grace-time settings.
how_to_obtain.command: config system global; show | grep 'admin-lockout-threshold\|admin-lockout-duration\|admin-ssh-grace-time'  (FortiGate). Harden: 'set admin-lockout-threshold 3', 'set admin-lockout-duration 300', 'set admin-ssh-grace-time 30'
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Non-zero lockout threshold + duration and short SSH grace time (secure) vs unset/zero (insecure)
how_to_obtain.source: FortiGate Hardening Guide — System administrator best practices

how_to_obtain.instruction: On non-FortiGate platforms, confirm the VPN-portal login enforces lockout/throttling via the IdP or local policy.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: A non-zero lockout threshold + duration is configured on both admin and VPN-portal login; no lockout / unlimited attempts is a finding.
how_to_obtain.source: general-knowledge

option_description: Whether authentication events (including failures) are forwarded to a central SIEM/syslog with failed-auth burst alerting and anomalous-session-source alerting enabled.
security_impact: An OR-trigger for both "Valid-account abuse / missing MFA" and "No connection / auth logging to SIEM"; fires (insecure) when logging is disabled/local-only or no failed-auth alerting exists.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Confirm authentication events are exported to a remote syslog/SIEM target.
how_to_obtain.command: show log syslog/forwarding config (FortiGate 'config log syslogd setting' -> 'set status enable' + server; PAN-OS log-forwarding profile to syslog)
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Remote syslog/SIEM target configured and enabled (secure) vs logging off or local-only (insecure)
how_to_obtain.source: FortiGate Hardening Guide — System administrator best practices

how_to_obtain.instruction: Confirm the SIEM raises alerts on failed-auth bursts and anomalous session sources for this gateway.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Log content and retention meet NIST SP 800-92; SIEM has detections for failed-auth bursts and anomalous session sources.
how_to_obtain.source: NIST SP 800-92 Guide to Computer Security Log Management

option_description: Which identity store the VPN authenticates against — a central IdP (RADIUS/SAML), LDAP directory, certificate CA, or local on-appliance accounts.
security_impact: An OR-trigger for "Valid-account abuse / missing MFA"; fires (insecure) on local_appliance_accounts, which permits shared/local accounts that bypass central MFA and lifecycle controls.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Read the authentication server / backend the VPN binds to.
how_to_obtain.command: show authentication server config (FortiGate 'config user radius'/'config user saml'; PAN-OS authentication-profile referencing RADIUS/SAML server-profile)
how_to_obtain.expected_output: External RADIUS/SAML/LDAP/cert server referenced (secure) vs local-user-db as the VPN auth source (insecure)
how_to_obtain.source: FortiGate Hardening Guide — System administrator best practices

how_to_obtain.instruction: Enumerate the authentication methods to confirm SSL-VPN uses a central directory/IdP/CA, not appliance-local accounts.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Authentication methods enumerated: certificate-based machine/user auth, RADIUS, SAML/OIDC federation, LDAP — confirm SSL-VPN uses one of these, not appliance-local accounts.
how_to_obtain.source: NIST SP 800-113 Guide to SSL VPNs

option_description: Attests that IKEv1 aggressive mode is disabled (IKEv2-only preferred). IKEv1 aggressive mode transmits the PSK hash in a way that exposes it to offline cracking.
security_impact: An OR-trigger for "Weak cryptography / downgrade"; the exposure fires when aggressive mode is still enabled (false).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Read the IKE phase1 version/mode configuration.
how_to_obtain.command: show vpn ike-sa / show running-config crypto ikev1|ikev2 (vendor-dependent: FortiGate 'config vpn ipsec phase1-interface' then 'show full-configuration | grep ike-version'; Cisco ASA 'show run crypto ikev1 | crypto ikev2')
how_to_obtain.expected_output: ike-version 2 (secure) vs ike-version 1 / aggressive mode keyword present (insecure)
how_to_obtain.source: NSA/CISA Selecting and Hardening Standards-based Remote Access VPN Solutions (2021)

how_to_obtain.instruction: Review the phase-1 proposals against NIST recommendations — IKEv2 required, IKEv1 aggressive mode and PSK-only auth flagged.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Phase-1 proposals reviewed against NIST SP 800-77r1 Appendix recommendations — IKEv2 required, IKEv1 aggressive mode and PSK-only auth flagged.
how_to_obtain.source: NIST SP 800-77r1 Guide to IPsec VPNs

option_description: Attests that weak encryption/integrity algorithms (DES, 3DES, MD5, SHA1) are removed from the accepted phase1/phase2 (and SSL-VPN) proposals in favour of AES-GCM/AES-256 and SHA-256+.
security_impact: An OR-trigger for "Weak cryptography / downgrade"; the exposure fires when weak ciphers remain accepted (false).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Read the accepted phase1/phase2 cipher/integrity proposals.
how_to_obtain.command: show running-config of phase1/phase2 proposals (e.g. FortiGate 'show vpn ipsec phase1-interface' -> proposal field; Cisco ASA 'show run crypto ipsec ikev2 ipsec-proposal')
how_to_obtain.expected_output: proposal aes256-sha256 / aes128gcm (secure) vs des-md5, 3des-sha1 (insecure)
how_to_obtain.source: NIST SP 800-77r1 Guide to IPsec VPNs

how_to_obtain.instruction: For the SSL-VPN portal, enumerate the offered ciphers on the wire to confirm no weak algorithms remain.
how_to_obtain.command: nmap --script ssl-enum-ciphers -p 443 <vpn-portal-host>
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Only TLSv1.2/TLSv1.3 with A-grade ciphers (secure); presence of SSLv3/TLSv1.0/TLSv1.1 or weak ciphers (insecure)
how_to_obtain.source: Nmap ssl-enum-ciphers NSE script

option_description: Attests that Perfect Forward Secrecy (PFS) is enabled on the IPsec phase2, so a compromised long-term key cannot decrypt past/future sessions.
security_impact: An OR-trigger for "Weak cryptography / downgrade"; the exposure fires when PFS is disabled (false).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Read the phase2 PFS and DH-group settings.
how_to_obtain.command: show phase2 PFS / dhgrp settings (FortiGate 'config vpn ipsec phase2-interface' -> 'set pfs enable' + 'set dhgrp 14 19 20'; Cisco 'show run crypto ipsec ... pfs group14')
how_to_obtain.expected_output: pfs enable + dhgrp 14/19/20 (secure) vs pfs disable or dhgrp 1/2/5 (insecure)
how_to_obtain.source: NIST SP 800-77r1 Guide to IPsec VPNs

how_to_obtain.instruction: Confirm PFS is enabled in the IPsec phase2 configuration per NIST IPsec guidance.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: PFS enabled on the IPsec phase2 (secure); PFS disabled is a finding.
how_to_obtain.source: NIST SP 800-77r1 Guide to IPsec VPNs

option_description: Attests that only strong Diffie-Hellman groups are accepted (DH group 14+/2048-bit or ECP group 19/20/21) and the weak groups 1/2/5 (768/1024/1536-bit) are not offered.
security_impact: An OR-trigger for "Weak cryptography / downgrade"; the exposure fires when a weak DH group is still enforceable/offered (false).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Read the accepted DH-group (dhgrp) settings on phase1/phase2.
how_to_obtain.command: show phase2 PFS / dhgrp settings (FortiGate 'config vpn ipsec phase2-interface' -> 'set pfs enable' + 'set dhgrp 14 19 20'; Cisco 'show run crypto ipsec ... pfs group14')
how_to_obtain.expected_output: pfs enable + dhgrp 14/19/20 (secure) vs pfs disable or dhgrp 1/2/5 (insecure)
how_to_obtain.source: NIST SP 800-77r1 Guide to IPsec VPNs

how_to_obtain.instruction: Confirm weak DH groups 1/2/5 are excluded and group 14+ or ECP 19/20/21 are enforced.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Only DH group 14+ (2048-bit) or ECP group 19/20/21 accepted; presence of group 1/2/5 (768/1024/1536-bit) is a finding.
how_to_obtain.source: NIST SP 800-77r1 Guide to IPsec VPNs

option_description: Minimum TLS version accepted on the SSL-VPN portal (GlobalProtect / FortiGate SSL-VPN / AnyConnect WebVPN / NetScaler Gateway).
security_impact: An OR-trigger for "Weak cryptography / downgrade"; fires when SSLv3/TLS1.0/TLS1.1 are still accepted ('tls1_0_or_tls1_1_or_sslv3_accepted'), enabling protocol downgrade and on-path interception.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Enumerate the TLS protocols offered by the SSL-VPN portal to determine the minimum accepted version.
how_to_obtain.command: nmap --script ssl-enum-ciphers -p 443 <vpn-portal-host>
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Only TLSv1.2/TLSv1.3 with A-grade ciphers (secure); presence of SSLv3/TLSv1.0/TLSv1.1 or weak ciphers (insecure)
how_to_obtain.source: Nmap ssl-enum-ciphers NSE script

how_to_obtain.instruction: Corroborate the offered protocols with testssl.sh against the portal.
how_to_obtain.command: testssl.sh https://<vpn-portal-host>:443
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Protocol section shows TLS 1.2/1.3 offered, older protocols 'not offered'; cipher categories show no NULL/EXPORT/DES/RC4
how_to_obtain.source: testssl.sh — Testing TLS/SSL encryption anywhere on any port

how_to_obtain.instruction: Confirm the configured cipher list matches a Mozilla Intermediate/Modern profile per NIST TLS guidance.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Configured cipher list matches Mozilla 'Intermediate' or 'Modern' profile; selection rationale documented per NIST SP 800-52r2.
how_to_obtain.source: NIST SP 800-52 Rev. 2 — Guidelines for the Selection, Configuration, and Use of TLS Implementations

option_description: Whether the gateway enforces a per-user/per-group least-privilege access policy that restricts which internal services and subnets an admitted session may reach (granular dst/service-scoped firewall rules from the VPN zone into the trust zone).
security_impact: An OR-trigger for "Flat internal access after admission"; fires when false (any admitted session reaches the whole internal network, enabling lateral movement).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Read the firewall policies from the VPN/SSL-VPN interface into internal trust zones.
how_to_obtain.command: show firewall policy from ssl.root/VPN interface to internal zones (FortiGate 'show firewall policy'; PAN-OS security rules with source zone = VPN)
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Granular dst-service-restricted rules per group (secure) vs single any-any rule from VPN zone to trust zone (insecure)
how_to_obtain.source: FortiGate Hardening Guide — System administrator best practices

how_to_obtain.instruction: Review that each user group maps only to the internal services it needs, with no permit-any from the VPN pool.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: VPN firewall/access policies reviewed: each user group maps to only the internal services it needs; no 'permit any any' from the VPN pool into internal zones.
how_to_obtain.source: NIST SP 800-46 Rev. 2 - Guide to Enterprise Telework, Remote Access, and BYOD Security

option_description: Whether a broad 'permit any-any' firewall rule exists from the VPN pool/SSL-VPN interface into internal trust zones, granting every admitted session flat reachability of the internal network.
security_impact: An OR-trigger for "Flat internal access after admission"; the insecure value is true (a permit-any rule collapses the segmentation the gateway is meant to enforce).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Review the firewall policy from the VPN interface for any broad source-VPN to dst-trust any-service allow.
how_to_obtain.command: show firewall policy from ssl.root/VPN interface to internal zones (FortiGate 'show firewall policy'; PAN-OS security rules with source zone = VPN)
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Granular dst-service-restricted rules per group (secure) vs single any-any rule from VPN zone to trust zone (insecure)
how_to_obtain.source: FortiGate Hardening Guide — System administrator best practices

how_to_obtain.instruction: Confirm no 'permit any any' rule exists from the VPN pool into internal zones.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: VPN firewall/access policies reviewed: each user group maps to only the internal services it needs; no 'permit any any' from the VPN pool into internal zones.
how_to_obtain.source: NIST SP 800-46 Rev. 2 - Guide to Enterprise Telework, Remote Access, and BYOD Security

option_description: Supporting context: whether downstream network segmentation (VLAN/zone separation, internal microsegmentation, or a segmentation firewall) constrains traffic originating from the VPN pool so even a broadly-permitted session cannot freely pivot across the trusted zone.
security_impact: Defense-in-depth contextual evidence for "Flat internal access after admission" (referenced by the rule but not its primary trigger); true indicates downstream containment limiting lateral movement.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Check for downstream segmentation constraining VPN-pool traffic within the trusted zone.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Downstream containment exists (VLAN/zone separation, microsegmentation, segmentation firewall) constraining VPN-pool traffic; flat reachability across the trust zone is a finding.
how_to_obtain.source: NIST SP 800-46 Rev. 2 - Guide to Enterprise Telework, Remote Access, and BYOD Security

how_to_obtain.instruction: From a host in the VPN pool, probe reachability across the trusted zone to confirm segmentation actually constrains pivoting.
how_to_obtain.command: From an admitted VPN client, attempt connections to internal subnets the user should not reach (e.g. 'nmap -sT <internal-segment-cidr>')
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Connections to out-of-scope internal segments are filtered/blocked (secure) vs broad reachability across the trusted zone (insecure)
how_to_obtain.source: general-knowledge

option_description: Whether the web/CLI admin interface (HTTPS/SSH) is reachable from the internet/WAN (e.g. allowaccess includes https/ssh on the external interface, admin bound to 0.0.0.0).
security_impact: The defining OR-trigger of "Internet-exposed management interface / default credentials"; fires when true — internet-exposed admin panels are the primary entry point for appliance RCE/auth-bypass CVEs.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Read the WAN interface allowaccess and admin bind/trustedhost configuration.
how_to_obtain.command: config system interface; edit <wan>; show full | grep allowaccess  (FortiGate). To harden: 'unset allowaccess' on external interface; restrict admins with 'config system admin' -> 'set trustedhost1 <cidr>'
how_to_obtain.expected_output: allowaccess on WAN has no https/ssh (secure) vs allowaccess includes https ssh on the external interface with no trustedhost restriction (insecure)
how_to_obtain.source: FortiGate Hardening Guide — System administrator best practices

how_to_obtain.instruction: From an external host, attempt to reach the admin port over the WAN IP.
how_to_obtain.command: From an external host: attempt to reach the admin port (e.g. 'curl -k https://<wan-ip>:<admin-sport>/')
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Connection refused/filtered from the internet (secure) vs admin login page served to arbitrary internet source (insecure)
how_to_obtain.source: CISA Enterprise VPN Security advisory (AA20-073A)

option_description: Whether the factory default admin password has been rotated and no vendor backdoor/maintenance accounts use shipped defaults.
security_impact: An OR-trigger for "Internet-exposed management interface / default credentials"; fires when false (default vendor credentials still valid).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Confirm the default admin password was rotated and no built-in/maintenance accounts use shipped defaults.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Confirm the default admin account password was rotated at install and credential-rotation is tracked; verify no enabled built-in accounts use shipped defaults.
how_to_obtain.source: CISA Enterprise VPN Security advisory (AA20-073A)

how_to_obtain.instruction: Enumerate configured admin accounts to verify none retain default usernames/credentials.
how_to_obtain.command: config system admin; show (FortiGate — review the admin account list); PAN-OS 'show admins' / Cisco ASA 'show running-config username'
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Admin accounts are uniquely named with rotated credentials (secure) vs default 'admin' account still using shipped defaults (insecure)
how_to_obtain.source: general-knowledge

option_description: Whether administrative access is restricted to trusted source IPs/CIDRs (e.g. FortiGate trustedhost, management ACL) rather than reachable from any source.
security_impact: An OR-trigger for "Internet-exposed management interface / default credentials"; fires when false — admin login served to arbitrary internet sources, enabling brute-force/default-credential attacks.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Read the trusted-host / management ACL restricting admin access source IPs.
how_to_obtain.command: config system interface; edit <wan>; show full | grep allowaccess  (FortiGate). To harden: 'unset allowaccess' on external interface; restrict admins with 'config system admin' -> 'set trustedhost1 <cidr>'
how_to_obtain.expected_output: allowaccess on WAN has no https/ssh (secure) vs allowaccess includes https ssh on the external interface with no trustedhost restriction (insecure)
how_to_obtain.source: FortiGate Hardening Guide — System administrator best practices

how_to_obtain.instruction: Confirm a trusted-host/management ACL is configured (FortiGate trustedhost, PAN-OS permitted-IP, Cisco management ACL).
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Admin access restricted to specific source IPs/CIDRs (secure); admin reachable from any source is a finding.
how_to_obtain.source: general-knowledge

option_description: Whether the gateway records VPN connect/disconnect and authentication events — both success and failure.
security_impact: An OR-trigger for "No connection / auth logging to SIEM"; fires when false (credential abuse and anomalous sessions leave no record).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Confirm event/auth logging is enabled and forwarded on the gateway.
how_to_obtain.command: show log syslog/forwarding config (FortiGate 'config log syslogd setting' -> 'set status enable' + server; PAN-OS log-forwarding profile to syslog)
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Remote syslog/SIEM target configured and enabled (secure) vs logging off or local-only (insecure)
how_to_obtain.source: FortiGate Hardening Guide — System administrator best practices

how_to_obtain.instruction: Inspect the gateway/SIEM logs to confirm VPN connect/disconnect and auth success+failure events are actually recorded.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: VPN connect/disconnect and authentication success and failure events appear in the log stream (secure); missing auth events is a finding.
how_to_obtain.source: NIST SP 800-92 Guide to Computer Security Log Management

option_description: Whether connection and authentication logs are exported off-box to a central SIEM/syslog target (not local-only).
security_impact: An OR-trigger for "No connection / auth logging to SIEM"; fires when false — a compromised gateway can impair its own local logging to evade detection (ATT&CK T1562.008) when records never leave the device.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Read the remote-syslog / log-forwarding configuration and confirm an off-box target is enabled.
how_to_obtain.command: show log syslog/forwarding config (FortiGate 'config log syslogd setting' -> 'set status enable' + server; PAN-OS log-forwarding profile to syslog)
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Remote syslog/SIEM target configured and enabled (secure) vs logging off or local-only (insecure)
how_to_obtain.source: FortiGate Hardening Guide — System administrator best practices

how_to_obtain.instruction: Confirm log content/retention and that the SIEM is actually receiving this gateway's logs.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Log content and retention meet NIST SP 800-92; SIEM has detections for failed-auth bursts and anomalous session sources.
how_to_obtain.source: NIST SP 800-92 Guide to Computer Security Log Management

option_description: Whether endpoint health/posture evaluation (AV present, OS patch level, disk encryption — e.g. a Host Information Profile / host-check policy) is configured and runs before VPN tunnel admission.
security_impact: An OR-trigger for "No client posture / device-compliance gating"; fires when false — any device with valid credentials is admitted into the trusted zone.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Check whether a host-check / Host Information Profile posture policy runs at tunnel admission.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Host-check / HIP (Host Information Profile) / compliance policy configured and enforced on the VPN portal; failing devices denied or quarantined.
how_to_obtain.source: NIST SP 800-46 Rev. 2 - Guide to Enterprise Telework, Remote Access, and BYOD Security

how_to_obtain.instruction: Read the posture/host-check configuration on the platform where it is exposed.
how_to_obtain.command: PAN-OS GlobalProtect: review HIP objects/profiles ('show global-protect-gateway ...' / Objects > GlobalProtect > HIP); FortiGate SSL-VPN: 'config vpn ssl web host-check-software' + portal host-check binding
how_to_obtain.expected_output: A posture/host-check policy (AV, OS patch, disk encryption) is bound to the VPN portal (secure) vs no posture evaluation configured (insecure)
how_to_obtain.source: general-knowledge

option_description: Whether the posture/compliance result is actually ENFORCED at admission — non-compliant or unmanaged devices are denied or quarantined rather than the check being advisory/log-only.
security_impact: An OR-trigger for "No client posture / device-compliance gating"; fires when gating is not enforced, so an unmanaged or compromised host reaches the internal network.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Verify that non-compliant/unmanaged devices are denied or quarantined at admission, not merely logged.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Host-check / HIP (Host Information Profile) / compliance policy configured and enforced on the VPN portal; failing devices denied or quarantined.
how_to_obtain.source: NIST SP 800-46 Rev. 2 - Guide to Enterprise Telework, Remote Access, and BYOD Security

how_to_obtain.instruction: Attempt admission from a deliberately non-compliant test device to confirm the posture result is enforced as a hard gate.
how_to_obtain.command: From a non-compliant test endpoint (e.g. AV disabled), attempt VPN tunnel admission and observe the result
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Non-compliant device is denied or quarantined at admission (secure) vs admitted with only a log entry / advisory warning (insecure)
how_to_obtain.source: general-knowledge

option_description: Whether a managed/enterprise device certificate is required as part of admission, distinguishing corporate-managed endpoints from arbitrary personal hosts presenting only user credentials.
security_impact: An OR-trigger for "No client posture / device-compliance gating"; fires when no managed-certificate requirement exists, allowing any credentialed device in.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Read the VPN authentication configuration for a required machine/device certificate alongside user credentials.
how_to_obtain.command: show authentication server config (FortiGate 'config user radius'/'config user saml'; PAN-OS authentication-profile referencing RADIUS/SAML server-profile) — and review certificate/machine-cert requirement on the portal/gateway
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Admission requires a managed/enterprise device certificate in addition to user credentials (secure) vs credentials-only admission (insecure)
how_to_obtain.source: FortiGate Hardening Guide — System administrator best practices

how_to_obtain.instruction: Confirm corporate-managed endpoints are distinguished by an enterprise-issued device certificate requirement at admission.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Authentication methods enumerated: certificate-based machine/user auth confirmed required for admission, not appliance-local credentials-only.
how_to_obtain.source: NIST SP 800-113 Guide to SSL VPNs
